title: Kenyan Pumpkin Soup
community: Urban Kenya — the hotel harvest season soup
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Pumpkin Soup — roasted orange-fleshed pumpkin blended with ginger, garlic, coconut milk, and warm spices into a vividly orange, silky, fragrant soup. The soup that showcases the colour and sweetness of Kenya's finest pumpkins.
longDesc: Pumpkin soup made from Kenya's orange-fleshed pumpkin varieties is a vivid, naturally sweet, deeply satisfying first course. The addition of coconut milk gives it a coastal character, and the ginger and spices give it warmth.
ingredients: 3 tbsp coconut oil or vegetable oil
Toasted pumpkin seeds and cream — to garnish
steps: Toss pumpkin, onion, and garlic with oil. Roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Transfer to a pot with ginger, stock, coconut milk, and spices.
Serve with a swirl of coconut cream and toasted pumpkin seeds.
chefTips: Roasting the pumpkin is the key step — boiled pumpkin soup is flat; roasted is extraordinary.
Blend while warm for the smoothest result.
Toasted pumpkin seeds (KEN156) make the perfect garnish.
commonMistakes: Boiling instead of roasting the pumpkin.
Under-seasoning — pumpkin needs generous salt and spices.
cookingScience: Roasting caramelises pumpkin's natural sugars, converting them from simple sweetness to complex caramel notes. The coconut milk emulsifies with the pumpkin puree during blending, producing a naturally silky texture without additional cream.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan pumpkins are among the most productive and drought-resistant crops.
healthBenefits: Exceptional beta-carotene — one serving provides 400% daily vitamin A.
culturalNote: Pumpkin soup in a Kenyan hotel demonstrates the culinary potential of crops that Kenyan farming communities have grown for generations — the same pumpkin whose leaves become mboga and whose seeds become snacks is also the base of an elegant restaurant soup.
